problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is defined as $⟨x,y⟩=2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ 
Calculate the norm of the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ under this inner product.

activity_context.topic_title: The Norm of a Vector in Inner Product Spaces

feedback.problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is defined as $⟨x,y⟩={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ 
Calculate the norm of the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ under this inner product.
feedback.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $v$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖=\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $‖v‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{2\cdot 2+2\cdot ((-1)\cdot (-1))+4\cdot 4} \\  & =\sqrt{4+2+16} \\  & =\sqrt{22}.\end{aligned}
$$
